name: Petrelintide

lead: Petrelintide is a weekly injectable amylin analogue from Zealand Pharma, partnered with Roche. It targets satiety rather than GLP-1 pathways.
A phase 1b trial reported 8.6 percent weight loss over 16 weeks; phase 2 results were published in 2026.

paras: It mimics amylin, a hormone that signals fullness after meals.
Investigational; safety data are in phase 1 and 2 publications. Not approved.

lead: Petrelintide (ZP8396) is an investigational once-weekly amylin analogue discovered by Zealand Pharma for weight management.[1][2] In March 2025 Roche entered a collaboration with Zealand to co-develop and co-commercialise it, alone and in combination with CT-388 (enicepatide).[1]

A phase 1b trial reported in June 2024 weight loss of 8.6 percent over 16 weeks.[1] A phase 2 trial, ZUPREME 1, has been published in The Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology, and phase 3 trials have begun recruiting.[3][4][5] It is not approved.

paras: Amylin is a satiety hormone released after eating, and petrelintide is a stable long-acting analogue of it; a medicinal chemistry paper describes its design.[2] Reviews describe amylin agonists as a potential class complementary to GLP-1 therapies.[6][7]

Two randomized, placebo-controlled phase 1 trials (single and multiple ascending dose) assessed safety, tolerability and pharmacokinetics.[8] The phase 2 ZUPREME 1 trial enrolled 493 people with obesity or overweight and comorbidities, and ZUPREME 2 enrolled 221 with type 2 diabetes.[3][4][9] Phase 3 trials totalling thousands of participants started in late 2026.[5] Numerical phase 2 results were not available in the sources reviewed.

timeline.event: Phase 1b result of 8.6 percent weight loss at 16 weeks announced.[1]
